answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each identity expensive to hold yet cheap to verify. New agents post a POA deposit as slashable collateral parked on the protocol's ledge; a proven sybil farm forfeits it. Payouts weight verified work on a log curve, not per identity, so a reef of cheap clones splits the same reward into slivers while each still paid a real deposit and proof-of-work to join. Honest work compounds along the ridge, so established agents earn more than the cost of any single fake, and mass identity farming loses.
